result.reviewScopeSummary: Initial verification of Story 3 against AC-6.1 through AC-6.3, the replay harness, corpus fixtures, verification tests, inspect/health evidence, and configured gates.

newFindings.title: Replay does not compare actual message and turn read-back records
newFindings.evidence: AC-6.1 requires the thread read-back — events, messages, and turns — to match fixture expectations. `replayCorpus` reads `intakeStream.listEvents` and `inspect.overview` only (`packages/pi-lhc/src/verify/replay.ts:282-291`). `compareReadback` compares event kind/payload order, then checks only `overview.messages.visible`, `overview.messages.byKind`, `overview.turns.closed`, and `overview.turns.open` (`packages/pi-lhc/src/verify/replay.ts:219-260`). The SDK exposes actual message and turn read-back surfaces (`messages` and `turns` exports in `packages/lhc/src/sdk.ts:1-4`, plus `MessageRecord`/`TurnRecord` types at `packages/lhc/src/sdk.ts:173-182`), but the Story 3 harness and tests do not consume them. `test/verify/replay.test.ts` adds an extra TC-6.1 assertion for event kinds only (`packages/pi-lhc/test/verify/replay.test.ts:86-91`). This leaves message content/order/turn association unverified despite the AC naming messages and turns explicitly.

newFindings.title: Corpus replay uses synthetic flat messages and inferred lifecycle instead of recorded PI hook corpora
newFindings.evidence: AC-6.1 is scoped to replaying recorded PI corpora. The fixture loader states that, until M0 delivers recordings, it builds synthetic stand-ins (`packages/pi-lhc/test/fixtures/corpus.ts:1-4`), and each named corpus source is an in-memory `AgentMessage[]` built with `makeUserMessage` / `makeAssistantMessage` (`packages/pi-lhc/test/fixtures/corpus.ts:21-29`, `42-53`, `69-83`, `97-105`, `118-124`). The replay harness source type is also just `AgentMessage[]` (`packages/pi-lhc/src/verify/replay.ts:35-38`). During replay it synthesizes deterministic entry ids and infers `agent_end` boundaries from a new user prompt or end-of-stream (`packages/pi-lhc/src/verify/replay.ts:117-143`) instead of consuming recorded `message_end` / `agent_end` events with their original positions. That proves the converter on synthetic message shapes, but not replay fidelity for recorded PI corpora or recorded lifecycle ordering.

verified: AC-6.2 / TC-6.2: deterministic replay and same-thread re-replay are covered by `test/verify/replay.test.ts`; full `pnpm --filter pi-lhc verify` passed with 79 tests.
AC-6.3 / TC-6.3: inspect overview/health counts, last event span, capture gaps, and failed derivations are covered by `test/verify/replay.test.ts`; full `pnpm --filter pi-lhc verify` passed.
Fixture validity risk for current fixture shapes: `test/fixtures/corpus.test.ts` validates well-formed expected event shapes and rejects a malformed corpus.
unverified: AC-6.1 / TC-6.1: actual `messages.listMessages` and `turns.listTurns` read-back records are not compared to fixture expectations.
AC-6.1 / TC-6.1: recorded PI corpus lifecycle replay is not proven; current corpus sources are synthetic flat `AgentMessage[]` inputs with inferred boundaries.

productionPathFindings: `packages/pi-lhc/src/verify/replay.ts` synthesizes entry ids and agent-run boundaries instead of replaying recorded hook lifecycle events, so the verification path is not yet proving recorded-corpus fidelity.
`packages/pi-lhc/src/verify/replay.ts` does not use the real message and turn read-back surfaces, only overview counts for those sections.
openQuestions: If M0 recorded corpora are still unavailable, does the impl lead want to explicitly accept synthetic stand-ins for this story, or should Story 3 remain blocked until those fixture inputs exist?
additionalObservations: Configured story gate `pnpm --filter pi-lhc verify` passed. `green-verify` failed only at `check-test-immutability.mjs` for four pre-existing Story 2 capture test files, matching the implementor's reported drift and not the configured Story 3 gate.
